description.narrative: The project is implemented in Palestine. The main outcome areas it contributes to are countering threat to democracy and human rights and opposing the backlash- increasing gender equality. The main rights holders are mainly rural women in five districts and indirectly their families, local communities and governorates. Through capacity building, campaigning, organizing of and through grassroots the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Health Development Information and Policy center (HDIP) and the Palme Center. The HDIP is originally a health organisation that now works closely with rural and local women, capacitating them to change their surroundnings, their communities and the judicial and political framework that are of their concern. They have a strong connection to grassroots and network between local activists in different locations.Other Donors to the OrganisationOther donors include FES and the Arab Fund. Coordination can be explored but is not a priority.Project ObjectiveTo achieve a greater diversity and representation in all levels of Palestinian life through community empowerment and grassroots-led efforts, with as special focusing on women and young women. This includes achieving legislative and policy changes on different levels of public authority and politics.Actor groupsRights-holders: Women and female youth in marginalized areas in five governates. Actors working in cooperation: womens associations and other CBOs in local communities. Umbrella network of grassroots womens associations. Decion-maker: informal community leaders, local authorities, national level legislators.
